key_insight: Pauli correlation encoding lets a variational quantum optimizer represent large binary problems with very few qubits by using correlator expectations as a continuous relaxation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a qubit-efficient path to large-scale power demand portfolio optimization, making hybrid quantum methods more relevant to real-world operational planning.
method: Encode binary decisions as Pauli correlation expectation values.
Use a two-stage hybrid workflow: time-averaged initialization followed by time-resolved optimization.
Map the optimization to a compact variational quantum circuit with continuous relaxation and discretization back to binary solutions.
evidence_signal: Simulations across problem sizes from 18 to 10,296 achieved near-optimal solutions with normalized cost gaps around 10^-4, and the approach remained robust on trapped-ion hardware.
watch_item: Solution quality depends on how well the correlator resolution translates continuous loss improvements into discrete decisions, so discretization effects and hardware noise remain important.
paper_title: Scalable Variational Quantum Optimization via Pauli Correlation Encoding: Application to Large-Scale Power Demand Portfolio Optimization
